scope: Original checked IR and local allocations survive preparation without cloning.
Captured source emits successfully after the file is replaced by invalid Rust; no second frontend pass occurs.
An unchanged retained build checks zero bodies; a one-body edit checks one.
Generic predicate environments remain the exact original slice.
Cold and warm abandoned preparations preserve artifacts; reverted and subsequent source builds run correctly.
Invalid source is rejected before emission and preserves the last executable.
Read/session failures and a real link failure remain failures; a later native request recovers.
Structs, references, a generic instance and a closure execute through ordinary native generation.

native_driver.includes: The seven owning-request tests, thirteen mixed admission/object tests and existing retained driver tests.

preserved_nonpassing_runs.name: initial owning API test run
preserved_nonpassing_runs.reason: The tests incorrectly equated has_out=true with emitted code. Generic templates intentionally have default empty FnOut and has_out=true. Tests were changed to inspect actual generated code; production code was unchanged.

preserved_nonpassing_runs.name: driver group without Cargo on PATH
preserved_nonpassing_runs.reason: Unchanged buildscript harness could not launch cargo.

preserved_nonpassing_runs.name: driver group with new Cargo build layout
preserved_nonpassing_runs.reason: Unchanged buildscript harness expected the previous output-file location. The declared compatibility layout environment restores its existing contract.

limits: This is the ordinary native prepare/emit ownership boundary, not a complete cross-implementation partitioner.
Standalone status-1 whole-source retry remains in src/main.rs.
Native frontend rejections still do not distinguish invalid Rust from missing native support; they never become complementary outcomes in this API.
No extra Rust frontend or new source classifier was added.
Imported FnAbi/layout integration and typed deferred semantic requests remain subsequent work.
No latency claim or new platform qualification is made.
